title: Erdos-Turan additive bases and representation growth

problemStatement.plain: Erdos #28 is the Erdos-Turan conjecture for additive bases of order 2: if A+A contains all sufficiently large integers, then the representation function r_A(n) should be unbounded. The Lean file formalizes the weak and strong conjectures, proves basic representation facts, and records known lower bounds as axioms.
whyMatters: Encodes a major additive-number-theory prize problem in representation-function language.
Separates elementary basis/counting lemmas from the still-open Erdos-Turan growth conjecture.

proven: `repFunc`, `repFuncUnordered`, `repFuncFinset`, `sumset`, and `IsAsymptoticBasis` define the representation and basis framework.
`isAsymptoticBasis_iff` relates the tail-coverage and finite-complement definitions of an additive basis.
`repFunc_pos_of_mem_sumset`, `sidon_repFunc_bounded`, and `sidon_density_bound` prove basic bounds and Sidon behavior.
`basis_element_count_sq` proves a counting lower bound on how many basis elements must appear up to N.
open: `grekos_lower_bound` and `borwein_lower_bound` are axiomatized known partial results.
The imported sharp Sidon infrastructure comes from the Erdos340 development.
knownResults.goal: Use the existing basis and Sidon lemmas to stage smaller representation-growth targets before attacking the full Erdos-Turan conjecture.
